head: d431cbef2a51144e61e0bb8b345f44ef7dbde4f3
summary:
I checked all 14 acceptance criteria against the committed tree (HEAD d431cbe) and every one holds.

**Python is gone.**
- `git ls-files` lists no *.py, *.pyc, *.pyw or *.pyi, including case-insensitive pathspecs. Nothing matches on disk either.
- The committed .gitignore holds `__pycache__/` and `*.pyc`, and git honours both with the global excludes file disabled.

**The same checks pass in a fresh scratch clone without Python.**
- In the clone, python, python3, py and pythonw cannot be resolved, and PYTHON*, HBAND_* and CHROME_BIN are unset.
- c7–c13 all exit 0. A planted tracked .py makes c7 exit 1, so it does catch one.
- `go build` passes, and `go test -count=1 -p 4 ./...` passes all 33 packages in 41 s.
- In the worktree with Chrome given, vet, build and the whole suite also pass (33 ok, 46 s).

**The ledger gates hold.**
- E-009 line 6 and line 7, run from bodies read read-only from the ledger, both PASS.
- The Edition probe, run against a fresh read-only copy of epics 39–44, finds 16/16 with 0 mismatches.
- I restored the six deleted .py files from 89da1ad in the clone and ran the probe again: it passes with all 6 present. So the deleted files are exactly what the Go port mapped.

**The launcher works when started with `go run`.** I drove it with a TCP poller that dials every 10 ms, the way look_web waits.
- The first connection came at 2.43 s. A GET sent on that first connection got 200 with 'continue this thread'.
- The `serving http://127.0.0.1:N/` line came at 2.44 s.
- `/`, `/reports`, the branch page and `/raw/e004-look` (98 bytes) all answered as they should, and the page shows '9 comments'.
- After the process tree was killed, nothing answered on N.
- The built binary exits 2 with the usage for `-port 0`, `0x1F90`, `abc` and a missing `-port`. Under `go run` the exit code is 1 with 'exit status 2', which is how go run reports it.

**The engine's Fitness check fires on planted files.** It flagged a planted .py under .taad and an `exec.CommandContext(t.Context(), "C:/Python314/PYTHON.EXE")` call. With both removed it is quiet again. The no-.py rule therefore matching no files on the real tree is the intended state.

**Still to do outside the repository:** the ledger's `projects.app_command` for project 14 still reads `python -I -X utf8 .taad/slices/SL-008/run_finish_e004_2.py serve --port {port}`, and that file is now deleted. Any look the engine runs in this worktree, or after the merge, will fail at launch until the engine sets it to `go run ./internal/testutil/seeded -port {port}`. That is an engine setting, not repository work, so it does not hold the slice.

Each kill of the launcher leaves 4 hband-* temp folders plus go-build folders, as the design accepts. I removed every one my runs left.

The slice's history shows no loop: one fork-measure send-back to the spike and one code-review fix that changed code.

The statement, cost and rollback the discharge promised are in place, and the tree has the Go launcher. The action it hands to the engine is NOT done: projects.app_command for id 14 still reads `python -I -X utf8 .taad/slices/SL-008/run_finish_e004_2.py serve --port {port}`, which names a deleted file. The engine must set `go run ./internal/testutil/seeded -port {port}`.

line 6 body PASS in the worktree; fresh-clone suite PASS

my own clone (gitdir inside the scratch folder) at d431cbe built and passed with Python off PATH
c10's pattern holds -[A-Za-z0-9] (it reads `py)(\.exe)?[[:blank:]]+(-[A-Za-z0-9]|...`), but I did not plant `py -3 x.py` to see it fire
TestPortFlagReadsADecimalPort passes; the real binary refuses -port 0x1F90 with 'is not a decimal number' and exit 2

not_reached: The engine's own look_web starting the app through projects.app_command. It still names the deleted Python script, so this was not exercised; a TCP poller of my own stood in for it.
TerminateJobObject was exercised only through E-009 line 7's test. My own kill was taskkill /T /F, a process-tree kill, not a job kill.
A real collision of the staging stand-in or staging hband with N was not forced; it is proven only by unit tests over the corpus.
A Ctrl+C stop of the launcher (signal path and the folder removal on it) was not driven on a real process.
Another Windows version, Linux or macOS were not tried; only this Windows 11 machine.
A fresh clone on a machine where Python was never installed was approximated by taking it off PATH; C:\Python314 still existed on disk.
